02 / Problem & approachOne savings journey

“How much can I
actually save?”

The customer knows the goal, but not the monthly amount. I focused on the point where a suggestion needs to become a decision: understanding whether the plan fits, changing it if it doesn’t, then authorising it.

“I want to save €3,000 for a holiday next summer, but I don’t know how much I can afford to save every month.”Example request from the challenge brief

I used conversation to capture the request and explain the assumptions. The plan then moves into a Savings Space with a timeline, amount controls and a review screen. Repeatedly asking the assistant to recalculate felt unnecessary when a control could show the result immediately.

Goal€3,000 for a holiday
Assumption€520 available each month
DeadlineAugust 2027

The financial figures are fictitious. AI replies are scripted in the prototypes; no bank account or model is connected.

04 / Design decisionsWhat I chose and why

Three decisions
behind the flow.

I kept the scope to the savings task. The main questions were how to explain the recommendation, how to let someone change it and when to ask for permission.

01

Use chat to capture
the goal.

The customer shouldn’t need to find a savings product first. After the initial request, I move the financial details into a visual plan. The original goal remains in context when switching between the conversation and the controls.

Request → explanation → Savings Space
I’d love a holiday next summer.
↓
Summer holiday€3,000 by August 2027
02

Show what changes
when you save less.

Eight transfers of €375 reach the goal in June, leaving €145 a month. Choosing €300 leaves €220, but needs ten transfers and finishes in August. Both meet the deadline. The choice is whether finishing early matters more than the extra €75 each month.

Same €3,000 goal; different monthly commitment
Monthly contribution€3,000 goal
€375 / monthJune 2027

€145 buffer

€300 / monthAugust 2027

€220 buffer

03

Ask for approval
after the review.

The review screen lists the account, amount, frequency, first transfer and final transfer. Confirmation stays disabled until the customer checks the approval box. Going back to edit the plan requires a fresh approval.

A recommendation does not authorise a transfer
REVIEW PLAN
First transfer1 November 2026
FrequencyMonthly, on the 1st

06 / Design-to-code handoffOpen Figma handoff ↗

ActionButton

I chose the button because its disabled state has a direct consequence: the customer must approve the plan before it can be created. This is the handoff specification; Code Connect was not configured for the exercise.

INTERACTIVE COMPONENT EXAMPLE

Disabled until approval is checked.

Inspect the Figma component ↗
<ActionButton
  label="Confirm plan"
  variant="primary"
  disabled={!approved}
  onClick={createSavingsPlan}
/>
Proposed API for a production component.
Component properties
PropertyTypeBehaviour
labelstringVisible action text and accessible name.
variantprimary | textPrimary action or lower-emphasis action.
disabledbooleanPrevents pointer and keyboard activation.
onClickcallbackRuns only when the button is enabled.
typebutton | submitMatches the surrounding form behaviour.
Geometry & type
52 px minimum height · 12 px radius · Inter Medium, 15/20 px. Use shared spacing and colour tokens.
States
Default, pressed and disabled; a visible focus ring for keyboard navigation. Text variant uses the same label and interaction rules.
Ownership
ReviewScreen owns approval. It passes disabled={!approved}. Editing the amount resets approval; the button must not keep its own copy of that state.
Production boundary
Approval enables submission. A real implementation still needs server validation, duplicate-submission protection and success/error feedback from the transfer service.
07 / AI-assisted workflowOpen workflow slide ↗

What changed
after the first version.

The initial execution looked unfinished. I kept the Savings Space and timeline, then asked for another pass on the hierarchy, palette, icons and component states. Both versions are preserved in Figma.

What I changed

  • Gave the monthly amount more space and a lighter type treatment.
  • Used a dark goal header and a white plan surface to separate the goal from the recommendation.
  • Kept the capacity, contribution and remaining buffer together.
  • Consolidated buttons, icons and approval states in the component library.

I checked the result against the task: can someone explain the amount, change it and tell what happens after confirming?

ToolWhat it generatedWhat I changed / checked
ChatGPT

Early journey options and a breakdown of the brief.

Selected one holiday savings journey. Kept chat for the request and explanation, with graphical controls for the decision.

Codex + Figma MCP

Editable Figma screens, foundations, components, variants and prototype wiring.

Rejected the first visual execution. Refined the hierarchy and brand treatment, reviewed screenshots and kept earlier versions in the archive.

Codex / web demo

The page, local financial calculations, interactive states and automated calculation checks.

Checked €375 and €300 scenarios, final transfer amounts, context after edits and the approval gate. Replayed the primary journey in the browser.

LIMITATIONS & NEXT ITERATION

No user research was conducted. I would test whether people understand “monthly capacity”, can explain the suggested amount and recognise that approval would create recurring transfers.

The prototype covers a regular monthly income. Variable income, insufficient funds and failed transfers need further design. The suggested “two months early” rule is a prototype assumption, not a validated recommendation model.
